body: EDIT: After looking at the numbers in both images closely, I realize I'm not printing out the actual position of the player capsule. Here are updated images including the player position. The X & Z coordinates are significantly closer to the target position with the patch. Release 4.4.1: Patched 4.4.1:

As mentioned in the linked PR, the `target_desired_distance` is not a last waypoint distance.

When a user sets a target position the system tries to find the closest valid position on navmesh to that position. The target position itself never changes and might be at the other end of the world so can never be reached at all. More common than not it hovers below or above the navmesh surfaces so is already an invalid target for distance checks. The actual waypoints are all on navmesh.

@smix8 If you look at the screenshots in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/108261#issuecomment-3034290516, you can see the target position is separate from the final position, which **is** in the navmesh.  We're also stopping short of that final position when the target_desired_distance < path_desired_distance.

Are you trying to say that the `target_desired_distance` is not intended to have any affect on how close the agent stops to the point returned by `final_position`?  Because that seems counter to how it is described in the docs:

https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/navigation/navigation_using_navigationagents.html
> At `target_desired_distance` from the target path position, the agent considers the target position to be reached and the path at its end.

Admittedly the docs say "target path position", but in reality its the navmesh point closest to the target path position.

Right now, we're stopping when within `path_desired_distance` of the final position.  Doesn't cause a problem when they're both 1.0, but it does when `target_desired_distance = 0.15`.

> Are you trying to say that the target_desired_distance is not intended to have any affect on how close the agent stops to the point returned by final_position?

Yes. There are old discussions to be found somewhere about all this. The gist is that movement and any "accuracy" regarding placement is a user responsiblity full-stop. Parts of the documentation likely need updating to drive that point home even more.

TL;DR: unexpected interaction with `path_height_offset` in `is_target_reachable()`, question at the bottom.

>  There are old discussions to be found somewhere about all this. The gist is that movement and any "accuracy" regarding placement is a user responsiblity full-stop

I'm confused here as to what the purpose of `target_desired_distance` is.  Do you have any links to those discussions.  I don't mind updating the documentation to reflect the intended behavior.

What's confusing me is that `target_desired_distance` is used in the code to check before finishing the navigation on one code path, but it's not on the other:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c6d130abd9188f313e6701d01a0ddd6ea32166a0/scene/3d/navigation/navigation_agent_3d.cpp#L867-L879

Wait a minute, this may actually be a strange interaction with `_is_target_reachable()`.  That was it!

Ok, I updated the MRP to use a Node3D instead of a CharacterBody3D.  I also updated the code to pick a point on the navmesh with `NavigationServer3D.map_get_closest_point()`.  When I set the NavigationAgent3D.target_position to a point I knew was on the navmesh, `is_target_reachable()` kept returning false.  
Updated MRP: [navigation-agent-finishes-early-issue.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21187989/navigation-agent-finishes-early-issue.zip)

**This was all because of a unexpected interaction of `is_target_reachable()` with `path_height_offset = -0.4`.**

The `path_height_offset` is applied in `get_final_position()` which is used by `is_target_reachable()` to test if its within `target_desired_distance`.  Because my `path_height_offset > target_desired_distance`, no point will ever be "reachable" with this NavigationAgent3D:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c6d130abd9188f313e6701d01a0ddd6ea32166a0/scene/3d/navigation/navigation_agent_3d.cpp#L745-L747

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c6d130abd9188f313e6701d01a0ddd6ea32166a0/scene/3d/navigation/navigation_agent_3d.cpp#L759-L765

There is a documentation change here for certain.  I'd like to expand the description for `target_desired_distance` to clarify that it does have an affect on when navigation finished, but only if the target position is reachable.  Otherwise, the waypoint distance is used to determine when the navigation finishes.

@smix8 One question for you, should `path_height_offset` be affecting the results of `_is_target_reachable()`?  If `target_position` is set to a point on the navmesh, should `_is_target_reachable()` always return true?

```gdscript
func set_movement_target(movement_target: Vector3):
    var map = get_world_3d().get_navigation_map()
    var nav_mesh_target = NavigationServer3D.map_get_closest_point(map, movement_target)
    navigation_agent.set_target_position(nav_mesh_target)
    print("Navigation to ", nav_mesh_target, " reachable ", navigation_agent.is_target_reachable())
```
